name: hex
description: Local-first voice dictation for macOS. Hold a shortcut, speak, and paste into any app. Native Rust, on-device speech recognition, and a Linux beta.
one_liner: A free Mac (and beta Windows/Linux) app that types what you say, fully offline — hold a shortcut, speak, release, and the text pastes wherever your cursor is, similar in spirit to Handy.
buyer: A Mac user who wants fast, private dictation and doesn't want to pay a monthly fee to a commercial dictation service like Wispr Flow or Superwhisper.
business_use_cases: A writer dictates drafts hands-free into any text editor without sending voice data anywhere.
A developer dictates commit messages, comments, or quick notes while their hands are busy with something else.

money_ideas.idea: Paid 'Modes' marketplace — pre-built text-processing presets for specific apps or professions sold as add-ons.
Enterprise deployment support for organizations rolling it out across many Macs.

steal_this: This space already has two strong free offline options trending the same week (this and Handy) — the real opportunity is a thin paid layer of custom vocabulary/macros, not another dictation app.
